NyxBridge
· by poqdavid

What it does

In managed mode VirtualAP hands the hotspot to an OpenWrt container and leaves its bridge, vap-br0, without an address, so the phone itself is not on the hotspot network. NyxBridge gives the phone an address there and adds the routing rule Android needs, so apps like LocalSend can reach hotspot devices.

It only acts while VirtualAP runs in managed mode, and removes everything it added when the hotspot stops.

Appearance

Theme
Following the device setting — currently light.
Material You
Use the colours from your wallpaper
Fullscreen
Hide the status and navigation bars

Credits

VirtualAP by ravindu644 creates the hotspot and the managed-mode bridge NyxBridge attaches to.

Droidspaces by ravindu644 runs the OpenWrt container that owns the hotspot network.

The idea of a low-priority routing rule for the hotspot subnet comes from studying droidspaces-lan-ip by yashoswalyo and VirtualAP’s routed mode. NyxBridge’s code is its own.

The WebUI shares its framework with NyxSUSFS and NyxProps. Issues and translations welcome.

7.hint: OpenWrt hands out .100–.249 by DHCP; keep the phone outside that range.

120.hint: Inside OpenWrt's DHCP range (.100–.249): a hotspot device could get the same address.
